findings.title: The dynamic imports are all started eagerly rather than on demand
findings.body: Each `import("./...")` expression is executed while the `appStore` object is initialized. Consequently, merely importing `@calcom/app-store` starts loading and evaluating every integration module, including integrations unrelated to the request. This defeats on-demand loading and keeps cold-start CPU, memory, and chunk-loading costs coupled to the full app catalog. Store loader functions instead (for example, `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`) and invoke only the selected loader at the call site.

findings.title: Calendar and video deletion promises are discarded during rescheduling
findings.body: `Array.prototype.forEach` does not await an async callback. The new `await getCalendar(...)` makes each calendar deletion asynchronous before `deleteEvent` is even invoked, but the surrounding `try/catch` exits immediately and the reschedule flow sends the email/returns without waiting for or observing any deletion failure. Rejections from either the import or provider call bypass this catch, and the old external event can remain active after the booking has been marked cancelled. Await a `Promise.all`/`Promise.allSettled` over `bookingRefsFiltered.map(...)`.

findings.title: Calendar and video deletion promises are discarded during rescheduling
findings.body: `Array.prototype.forEach` does not await an async callback. The new `await getCalendar(...)` makes each calendar deletion asynchronous before `deleteEvent` is even invoked, but the surrounding `try/catch` exits immediately and the reschedule flow sends the email/returns without waiting for or observing any deletion failure. Rejections from either the import or provider call bypass this catch, and the old external event can remain active after the booking has been marked cancelled. Await a `Promise.all`/`Promise.allSettled` over `bookingRefsFiltered.map(...)`.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation does not wait for calendar deletions
findings.body: The async callback passed to `forEach` is never joined. In this branch it now first awaits `getCalendar`, so the parent handler can reach its later `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` before the callbacks have populated `apiDeletes`; those callbacks push the deletion result only after the deletion has already completed. The handler can therefore remove booking references and return success while recurring external calendar events are still being deleted, and provider/import failures become unhandled. Build and await a promise per credential/booking deletion instead of using `forEach`.

findings.title: Request-reschedule returns before integration deletions finish
findings.body: The async callback supplied to `forEach` is discarded. Since the calendar branch now awaits `getCalendar`, neither the calendar import nor `deleteEvent` is awaited by the mutation, and there is no rejection handler for either operation. The booking is already marked cancelled and the mutation can complete while its calendar/video event remains active; a failed dynamic import or provider deletion is an unhandled rejection. Await a collected `Promise.all`/`Promise.allSettled` for these callbacks before completing the reschedule operation.
